title: Undertow is live: 112 fishing horror sounds, from the wrong bite to the abyss
body:
Undertow: Fishing Horror Sound Effects is out. 112 sounds in WAV and OGG for a fishing game where something is down there: the cast into the dark, the wrong bite, a line that pulls back harder than any fish, what comes up on the hook, and the small boat at night. It takes Slackwater, our calm fishing pack, into a horror game, in the same grammar: one rig, placed on a water, and the relations a game asks for made measurable.

Four events on five dread waters. The lure landing, the wrong bite, a breach beside the boat and the float pulled under, each on black lake, fog sea, ice hole at night, black swamp and open water over a trench. 70 pairs of cells that differ in one thing were compared from the shipped files, each at least 9% apart in brightness or 18% in length. Failing pairs: 0. Each water also ships as a seamless bed.

4 ladders: the line pulled back at four strengths (each its own loop length, so a game crossfades as the tension climbs), the catch reveal from ordinary to odd to aberrant to abyssal, a knock on the hull from far off to directly beneath, and the fish finder return from a small fish to something impossibly large. 12 steps checked, every one moving the declared way by at least 8%, every ladder at least 1.5x end to end.

4 whole lifecycles (the reel, the outboard, the anchor chain and the lantern: start, loop, stop and fail) with 24 state pairs compared and none alike, and the dread as three loops of one length that stack: the night on the water, then something under the boat, then it is circling, summed and checked at all 3 levels. 20 loops in all, loop points written into the WAV and the OGG.

Already own Slackwater? Every file here was compared against every file in Slackwater and in 5 more of our packs (84224 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 84224 of 84224 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download.

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Everything is synthesised from code, so there are no samples and no upstream licence behind it. There is a free demo of 18 sounds on the page: the catch reveal at all four levels, the wrong bite on every water, the hull knock from far to beneath, the lantern's every state and the black lake as a bed. Listen before you buy; that is what it is for. 1040 checks, 0 failed, and the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.34 dB of loudness.

Made by Core Systems Asset Factory. The code and the cover are AI assisted; the sounds are not: every one is procedural synthesis written in code, with no generative audio model anywhere in the pipeline. There are no creature voices and nothing musical. Nobody claims these sound good; the figures above are signal measurements.
